hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: If deleting any single case-29 declaration moves the frame by 4 rather than 0 or 8, the 8-byte charge does not hold inside a switch-arm overlay and the per-candidate ruler is the wrong tool.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - `slotdiff.py game/sfx/sfx StartExplosion` shows the four live local slots shifted uniformly (+48 at 24/28/32, +40 at 48) with no exclusive local slot of our own, which is the signature of a pure overlay-size surplus rather than a placement defect.
hypothesis.statement: The case-29 overlay region is sized by the arm's HOMED declarations only, not by its declaration count, so the next lane must identify WHICH of case 29's fourteen declarations acquire stack homes before deleting any. The cheap discriminant is the 8-byte ruler applied per candidate: add `u8 _probe8[8]` and note the frame moves 16; then delete one candidate and note whether the frame moves 8 (homed scaffold) or 0 (register-resident). Our live slots sit at 72/76/80/88 against target 24/28/32/48, so exactly 48 bytes of overlay - six homed declarations at the 8-byte charge - have to go.
